  • Architecture
    • Architecture Decisions
      • ADR Template
      • 001. Keep one monorepo for every stack
      • 002. Modules are removable as whole slices
      • 003. Every project documents itself
      • 004. One shared domain model serves streaming and storage
      • 005. Development infrastructure starts with the app that needs it
      • 006. The whole system runs on one machine
      • 007. One shared identity provider serves every authenticated surface
      • 008. Real secrets are encrypted; only dev defaults are committed
      • 009. Every example runs and is tested, or it is removed
      • 010. The unit validated is the unit that ships
      • 011. The development environment is a versioned artifact
      • 012. Validation runs against real services, not substitutes
      • 013. Services prove who they are at every boundary
      • 014. The gate that refuses a change is defined once
      • 015. A change answers for what it caused; the state of the world is reviewed on a cadence
      • 016. The system observes itself; its operational data never leaves it
      • 017. Shared concepts change only in ways that keep readers working
      • 018. Settings arrive at startup through one channel and fail loudly
      • 019. The system releases as one versioned whole
      • 020. Dependencies stay current by default; majors move by decision
      • 021. A new technology joins the system by recipe
      • 022. The codebase explains itself to the agents that change it
      • 023. A storage schema changes only by recorded migration
      • 024. A validated release is promoted by a declared path
      • 025. Data has a stated lifetime that the system enforces
      • 026. The system can be brought back from a named snapshot
      • 027. Every stream carries a stated delivery guarantee
      • 028. Operational secret handling has a named owner and a rehearsed path
      • 029. What ships is signed, and its origin can be proven
      • 030. Interfaces between parts are verified, not assumed
      • 031. Language and runtime versions have a declared support window
      • 032. Shared streams are named by a declared convention
      • 033. Shipped artifacts carry a contents inventory
      • 034. Signals meet at one replaceable collection point
      • 035. Parts hand work to each other through a durable event log
      • 036. The delivery plane is a named exception to the data boundary
      • 037. The system itself promises nothing about staying up
      • 038. What a person may do is decided in one place, apart from who they are
      • 039. Data is protected where it travels and where it rests
      • 040. The system raises its hand when it is broken
      • 041. A failure of the running system has an owner and a rehearsed path
      • 042. Every dataset has an owner who answers for it
      • 043. AI-assisted review informs the two signatures
      • 044. Every change carries two human signatures
      • 045. Conventions are borrowed before they are invented
      • 046. The catalogue keeps its public contract
      • 047. One search store is the system of record
      • 048. Behaviour is proven against the reference
      • 049. Every function and rule is traceable to a test
      • 050. The system carries only what the catalogue needs
      • 051. The conversion proceeds in specified increments
      • 052. Behaviour is specified by scenarios read from the reference source
      • 053. The webapp is rewritten in Angular idiom, slice by slice
      • 054. The server API is the webapp's one data plane
      • 055. The lineage chain is a named data surface

aurelius-atlas-model¶

Atlas data shapes for Aurelius Atlas, without I/O (DD-002). Since increment 1.1: the Apache Atlas 2.4.0 type definitions (enum, struct, classification, entity, relationship and business metadata), their header and AtlasTypesDef, as Pydantic models that read and write Atlas's REST JSON. Since 1.5: the patch record AtlasPatch.

from aurelius_atlas_model.typedef import AtlasTypesDef

types = AtlasTypesDef.model_validate(request_body)  # Atlas's normalisations apply
response_body = types.to_json()  # Java names, nulls left out, epoch-millisecond dates

Installation¶

dependencies = ["aurelius-atlas-model"]

[tool.uv.sources.aurelius-atlas-model]
workspace = true

Documentation¶

aurelius_atlas_model.typedef ¶

Atlas type definitions as Pydantic models that read and write Atlas's REST JSON (DD-020).

Ported from org.apache.atlas.model.typedef of Apache Atlas 2.4.0. Field names are snake_case in Python and the Java getter names in JSON (TDM-01). The normalisations the Java setters and constructors apply run as validators, so they hold for request bodies and for models built in code alike.

Type Aliases:

  • AttributeDefs –

    attributeDefs: never null, one definition per name (TDM-06, TDM-07).

  • JavaBool –

    A Java boolean: an explicit null reads as false (TDM-10).

  • JavaInt –

    A Java int: an explicit null reads as 0 (TDM-10).

  • NameSet –

    A Java Set<String> that is never null (TDM-06, TDM-09).

  • OptionalNameSet –

    A Java Set<String> that may be null (TDM-09).

  • Timestamp –

    A java.util.Date: an aware datetime, written as epoch milliseconds (TDM-05).

Classes:

  • AtlasAttributeDef –

    An attribute of a struct, classification, entity, relationship or business metadata type (TDM-10).

  • AtlasBaseTypeDef –

    What every type definition has: identity, audit fields, name and options.

  • AtlasBusinessMetadataDef –

    A business metadata type: attributes that apply to the entity types its options name.

  • AtlasClassificationDef –

    A classification type: attributes, super types and the entity types it may be applied to.

  • AtlasConstraintDef –

    A constraint on an attribute, such as ownedRef or inverseRef.

  • AtlasEntityDef –

    An entity type.

  • AtlasEnumDef –

    An enum type.

  • AtlasEnumElementDef –

    One value of an enum type.

  • AtlasModel –

    The JSON conventions of every Atlas model (TDM-01 to TDM-03, TDM-15, DD-020).

  • AtlasRelationshipAttributeDef –

    An entity attribute that a relationship type adds; read-only, derived from the relationship types.

  • AtlasRelationshipDef –

    A relationship type between two entity types (TDM-12).

  • AtlasRelationshipEndDef –

    One end of a relationship type: the entity type there and the attribute it gets (TDM-12).

  • AtlasStructDef –

    A struct type, and the base of the types that have attributes.

  • AtlasTypeDefHeader –

    The identity of a type definition, as /v2/types/typedefs/headers lists it.

  • AtlasTypesDef –

    Type definitions of every kind: the body of /v2/types/typedefs (TDM-13).

  • Cardinality –

    How many values an attribute or relationship end holds.

  • IndexType –

    How an attribute is indexed.

  • PropagateTags –

    The direction in which classifications propagate over a relationship.

  • RelationshipCategory –

    How the two ends of a relationship depend on each other.

  • TypeCategory –

    The kinds of Atlas types (org.apache.atlas.model.TypeCategory).

Functions:

  • array_type_name –

    The name of the array type of element_type_name: array<T> (TDM-19).

  • find_attribute –

    The first attribute definition named name, compared without case, or None (TDM-16).

  • map_type_name –

    The name of the map type from key_type_name to value_type_name: map<K,V> (TDM-19).
